newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke backs free vote on Europe issues.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke backs free vote on Europe issues.

text.p: Britain's former finance minister Kenneth Clarke, a contender for the leadership of the defeated Conservative Party, said on Sunday he favoured a free vote for his divided party on all major European issues.
"Let us stop this obsession with Europe," Clarke said on BBC television. "What we mustn't allow is zealots inside the party...to turn the whole leadership election into a pro- and anti-Europe thing."

Clarke, on the left of his party, said he would go further than outgoing party leader John Major, who offered Conservatives a free vote on joining a European single currency before he lost the prime ministerhip in last Thursday's election.
"I would extend that (free vote) to major European issues," Clarke said. "There must be an understanding that there is a free vote on big critical issues."

He said the Conservatives had to convince the British people they were able to govern again and that he planned to do that, if successfully elected to head the party, by making Europe an open issue rather than trying to paper over the differences.
"It's a kind of cancer at the heart of the party," he said of the Conservatives' long-running divisions over Britain's ties with the European Union.

Clarke, a leading Conservative proponent of integration with the EU, said he was shocked and sorry that former Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine had ruled himself out of the leadership race due to health problems.
"He has been a great political ally of mine," Clarke said of his fellow moderate. "He's got courage, he's got flair."
